title: Run-loop probabilistic semantics
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ bound the space used by $N$ on every input and every choice word. Let $n,\ell,S,K,B\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $os$ be a Boolean. Suppose $N$ uses at most $sp(|x|)$ space on every such run, $sp(|x|)\le S$, the configuration-code bound for $N$, $|x|$, and $S$ is at most $K$, and $n+\ell+S+2K+2\le B$. For every $i,cnt,c,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $cnt+i\le K+1$, $c\le K$, and $d\le K$, the amplifier started at its run-loop label with registers initialized from $(n,\ell,S,K,i,cnt,c,d,0)$ terminates for every sequence of choice bits, keeps each register at most $B$ while running, and has acceptance probability equal to the fraction of uniformly random choice words of length $iK$ for which the decision rule applied to $cnt$ plus the number of accepting length-$K$ blocks is true.
